name: Jewish secularism
summary: Jewish secularism holds that being Jewish is a matter of peoplehood, history and culture rather than belief, so Jewish life can be lived without God or religious authority. It rests on secular Jewish thought and institutions (Humanistic Judaism, the Bund's Yiddish culture) and on Israeli secularism (hilonim, Hiddush), which want religion kept out of the state: civil marriage, public transport on Shabbat, equal military service and equal treatment of every stream of Judaism. It values Jewish culture and languages, democracy and Israel as the achievement of secular Zionism, while its strands differ on Zionism, diaspora autonomy and settlement policy.
scope: Jewish identity, culture and peoplehood without religious belief, as held by secular Jewish thought and institutions (Humanistic Judaism and its federation, the Society for Humanistic Judaism and its religion-state initiative, the Congress of Secular Jewish Organizations, secular Yiddishist and Hebrew culture with the Bund as historical background) and by Israeli secularism (the hiloni public, Hiddush) on religion and state. A position of a movement body counts only when its sources tie it to being secular or Jewish (church-state separation, Jewish identity and culture, religious exemptions, Israel); generic progressive resolutions on guns, drugs, immigration and similar are left unanswered, and the abortion, LGBT and assisted-dying positions are kept at medium only because the movement's own resolutions and JFASD state them. Excludes secular-universalist and anti-Zionist Jews (Liebman and Yadgar's term), who are indifferent to Jewish peoplehood, and religious movements.

sources.title: The Commitments of Secular Humanistic Jews (1986 proclamation)
sources.author: International Federation of Secular Humanistic Jews
sources.usedFor: Founding proclamation: reason, Jewish identity as ethnic reality, secular humanistic democracy, separation of religion and state, privacy and moral autonomy, equal rights regardless of race, sex, creed or ethnic origin.

sources.title: Statement of Principles, Eighth Biennial Congress (2000)
sources.author: International Federation of Secular Humanistic Jews
sources.usedFor: Ten commitments: reason, justice, Jewish culture and languages, pluralism, openness (democracy, equality of men and women, peace); Zionism and Israel as the secular Jewish achievement.

sources.title: LCSHJ Resolutions (intermarriage 1991, aid in dying 1995, circumcision 2002, sexual and gender diversity 2004)
sources.author: Leadership Conference of Secular and Humanistic Jews, hosted by IISHJ
sources.usedFor: Right to choose marriage partners, interfaith weddings, aid in dying, legal equality for LGBT people.

sources.title: Jews for a Secular Democracy
sources.author: Society for Humanistic Judaism
sources.usedFor: The movement's religion-state initiative: neutral government, no religious exemptions to discriminate, secular curricula, reproductive and LGBTQ rights grounded in secular and Jewish values.

sources.title: The Hiddush Vision: Imagine a Reality
sources.author: Hiddush: For Religious Freedom and Equality
sources.usedFor: Israeli secular religion-and-state agenda: civil marriage, voluntary religious courts, equal treatment of all streams, equal military service, common school core, Shabbat public transport, gender equality.

sources.title: Hiddush survey for International Human Rights Day
sources.author: Hiddush
sources.usedFor: Survey: 94% of secular Israelis back Shabbat public transport, 93% civil marriage and divorce.

sources.title: Secular-Jewish Identity and the Condition of Secular Judaism in Israel
sources.author: Charles S. Liebman and Yaacov Yadgar (Bar-Ilan / BJPA)
sources.usedFor: Scholarly typology of Israeli secularism: secular-Judaists versus secular-universalists; hostility to religious coercion; Hebrew and Zionist secularisation.

sources.title: Israel's Religiously Divided Society (Pew Research Center survey of Israeli Jews, 2014-15)
sources.author: Pew Research Center
sources.usedFor: Views of the Hiloni (secular) fifth to half of Israeli Jews on halakha as law, Shabbat transport, civil marriage, expulsion of Arabs, two states, settlements, aliyah, Jewish identity.

sources.title: Opposing school vouchers (2012)
sources.author: Society for Humanistic Judaism
sources.usedFor: Opposes vouchers and tax credits that fund religious schools, on church-state grounds.

sources.title: Supporting an international bill opposing blasphemy laws (2015)
sources.author: Society for Humanistic Judaism
sources.usedFor: Supports repeal of blasphemy laws: free speech includes the freedom to criticise religions.

sources.title: In Support of Workers' Rights (2011)
sources.author: Society for Humanistic Judaism
sources.usedFor: Fair wage, safe conditions, right to form unions, collective bargaining where necessary; cites Jewish tradition on treatment of workers.

sources.title: Supporting reproductive choice as a fundamental right (1996)
sources.author: Society for Humanistic Judaism
sources.usedFor: Moral and legal right to decide on ending a pregnancy; right to control one's own body; no group may use its beliefs to override it.

sources.title: Enforcing secular curricula in public, private and parochial schools (2016)
sources.author: Society for Humanistic Judaism
sources.usedFor: Governments should require and enforce core secular instruction and reject religious exemptions.

sources.title: Supporting science teaching in public schools (2007)
sources.author: Society for Humanistic Judaism
sources.usedFor: Scientific inquiry as the only rational basis for understanding the world; unscientific content should not intrude into publicly funded science teaching.

sources.title: Opposing a school prayer constitutional amendment (1995)
sources.author: Society for Humanistic Judaism
sources.usedFor: Opposes school prayer as a breach of church-state separation.

sources.title: Who is a Jew? (1988 resolution)
sources.author: International Federation of Secular Humanistic Jews / Society for Humanistic Judaism
sources.usedFor: A Jew is a person of Jewish descent or anyone who declares themselves Jewish and identifies with the people; conversion unnecessary; welcome intermarried families.

sources.title: Statement on sexual ethics for the 21st century (2018)
sources.author: Association of Humanistic Rabbis (hosted by SHJ)
sources.usedFor: Consent as the main standard, decriminalising consensual adult sex including sex work, freedom for monogamous or polyamorous relationships.

sources.title: Supporting marriage rights for same-sex couples (2004)
sources.author: Society for Humanistic Judaism
sources.usedFor: Legal recognition of same-sex marriage and divorce; equal rights and responsibilities in marriage.

sources.title: Supporting Israel's right and responsibility to defend its citizens (2002)
sources.author: Society for Humanistic Judaism
sources.usedFor: Supports Israel's defence and a negotiated settlement with a demilitarized sovereign Palestinian state.

sources.title: General Statement on Israel (2014)
sources.author: Society for Humanistic Judaism
sources.usedFor: Israel's creation as a major accomplishment of the Jewish people, secular roots, support for a peace process and the Declaration of Independence's equality.

sources.title: Israel statements and resolutions (index)
sources.author: Society for Humanistic Judaism
sources.usedFor: SHJ says its members hold views from ardent Zionist to anti-Zionist, with no consensus.

sources.title: Zionism and Humanistic Judaism
sources.author: Sherwin Wine (founder of Humanistic Judaism)
sources.usedFor: Wine on Zionism, Hebrew revival, Israel as cultural homeland, Jews as a nation, Diaspora without assimilation.

sources.title: Declaration of the Establishment of the State of Israel (1948)
sources.author: Provisional State Council (text via Yale Avalon Project)
sources.usedFor: Founding text of the secular Zionist state: open to Jewish immigration, equal rights irrespective of religion, freedom of conscience, offer of peace.

sources.title: Bund, Jewish (Encyclopedia of Modern Europe)
sources.author: Robert Weinberg, via Encyclopedia.com (Gale)

notes: Re-audited 2026-10-29 from scratch. The earlier audit took the SHJ's resolutions on unrelated issues as the ideology's positions; those are now null unless a source ties them to secularism or Jewishness (guns, cannabis and drugs, immigration, hate speech, taxes). Themes searched: economy (workers' rights only), government (democracy; no position on courts, elections or federalism), world (Israel, peace, aliyah, Diaspora), liberty, society, culture, ecology and technology (nothing found). Diaspora humanists and Israeli secularists differ on security, settlements and the Law of Return; secular Yiddishists, secular Zionists and anti-Zionist Jews split on national-cultural autonomy and Zionism, so those are 0 or low. Hiddush backs freedom of and from religion but not necessarily full separation; the federation and JFASD state separation outright.
